question.prompt:
A ray of light originates from point \(A\) and travels in a plane, being reflected \(n\) times between lines \(AD\) and \(CD,\) before striking a point \(B\) (which may be on \(AD\) or \(CD\)) perpendicularly and retracing its path to \(A.\) (At each point of reflection the light makes two equal angles as indicated in the adjoining figure. The figure shows the light path for \(n=3.\)) If \(\angle CDA=8^\circ,\) what is the largest value \(n\) can have?

[Figure 1](figures/1981_AMC_12_Q20_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The useful quantity is the angle between each arriving segment and the boundary ray pointing toward \(D\). The reflection law lets us track this angle from one contact to the next.

Write \(R_0=A\), let \(R_1,\ldots,R_n\) be the ordinary reflection points, and write \(R_{n+1}=B\) for the final perpendicular contact. These contacts alternate between the two sides of the \(8^\circ\) wedge shown. Define
\[
\beta_j=\angle DR_jR_{j-1}.
\]
At an ordinary reflection, the two path segments make equal angles with the boundary line. Consequently, their angles with the same boundary ray \(R_jD\) are supplementary: the outgoing angle \(\angle DR_jR_{j+1}\) is \(180^\circ-\beta_j\).

In \(\triangle DR_jR_{j+1}\), the angle at \(D\) is \(8^\circ\). Its angle sum therefore gives
\[
8^\circ+(180^\circ-\beta_j)+\beta_{j+1}=180^\circ,
\]
so
\[
\beta_{j+1}=\beta_j-8^\circ.
\]
There are \(n\) such steps from the first contact to the final contact. Since the final strike is perpendicular, \(\beta_{n+1}=90^\circ\), and hence
\[
\beta_1=90^\circ+8^\circ n.
\]
Let \(\alpha=\angle DAR_1\) be the launch angle into the wedge. The first triangle, \(\triangle DAR_1\), gives
\[
\alpha+8^\circ+\beta_1=180^\circ.
\]
A nondegenerate path has \(\alpha>0\), so \(\beta_1<172^\circ\). Thus
\[
90+8n<172,
\qquad n<10.25.
\]
Since \(n\) is an integer, \(n\le10\).

To show that ten reflections are possible, launch the ray at \(\alpha=2^\circ\) toward the opposite side. The first incoming angle is \(170^\circ\), and successive incoming angles are
\[
170^\circ,162^\circ,154^\circ,\ldots,98^\circ,90^\circ.
\]
Each intermediate contact exists on the opposite boundary ray: the next triangle has angles \(8^\circ\), \(180^\circ-\beta_j\), and \(\beta_j-8^\circ\), all positive. The first ten contacts are ordinary reflections, and the eleventh is perpendicular. The light then retraces its path by the same reflection law. Therefore the largest value is \(\boxed{10}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Track the angle at each contact
